dispersion.basis: Ratios of each state's and each household expenditure quintile's private-hospital mean to its own all-India figure (NSS 75th round, Tables A17, A18 and A29), combined across the two axes on an assumption of independence. These are spreads between stratum means, not between individual bills; the survey publishes no patient-level quantile anywhere.

excludes: The survey's expenditure figures exclude childbirth, which is carried separately, and exclude transport, food and lodging throughout.

multiplier.basis: Private charge estimated at 3.37x the government tariff, from the one ailment category where the survey and the tariff price the same event: private-hospital expenditure on a delivery (NSS 75th round, Table A29, deflated to December 2025) against the mean of the two PM-JAY delivery packages. The same ratio computed for the other categories ranges from 0.79 (cardio-vascular) to 4.02 (respiratory), but those compare a survey average over admissions with an unweighted average over catalogue rows, which are different populations; they are reported as evidence, not used. One category is one observation.

denominator.childbirth: mean tariff of the 2 ClaimCast procedure(s) coded as childbirth, because Obstetrics and Gynecology mixes deliveries with gynaecological surgery
denominator.gastro-intestinal: mean of 177 packages in SG, loosely mapped: General Surgery is mostly abdominal but also carries hernias, thyroids and varicose veins
denominator.infections: mean tariff of the 1 ClaimCast procedure(s) coded as infections, because Infectious Diseases holds four packages, too few to average
denominator.psychiatric-neurological: mean of 85 packages in SN/MM, loosely mapped: Neurosurgery and Mental Disorders together, which is the survey's own pairing but an unusual one for a tariff
denominator.respiratory: mean tariff of the 1 ClaimCast procedure(s) coded as respiratory, because pneumonia sits in General Medicine, which is 159 packages of everything

split.basis: NSS Statement 3.17, private hospitals, by sector. The bundled `package` component -- 40% of the urban private bill -- is not itemised by the survey and is redistributed across the itemised components in their own proportions.
